newsitem.title: CANADA: Thai banker's extradition hearing to face delay.
newsitem.headline: Thai banker's extradition hearing to face delay.

text.p: A Canadian judge said on Wednesday the extradition trial of a former Thai bank official accused of embezzlement would be adjourned until September.

British Columbia Supreme Court Justice Frank Maczko has heard more than a week of arguments in the case against Rakesh Saxena, former treasury advisor to the Bangkok Bank of Commerce who is charged in Thailand with embezzling about $65 million from the bank.
But the judge and lawyers representing both Saxena and Thailand agreed on Wednesday they would not be able to complete the proceeding by the end of the week as planned, forcing an adjournment.
Because of scheduling difficulties, the case would not be able to resume until mid-to-late-September, Maczko said. He plans to finalise arrangements over the next few days.
Saxena, an Indian citizen and former resident of Thailand, was arrested nearly a year ago by Canadian and Thai police at the Whistler mountain resort near Vancouver.

Thailand's extradition effort has already faced numerous delays. The hearing has been prolonged by disputes over the admissibility of a host of evidence, notably testimony from witnesses and officials in Thailand.
Judge Maczko told the court on Wednesday he would spend the day reviewing submissions and then take up the issue of their admissibility during the rest of the week before adjourning the case.
The Thai government took over the Bangkok bank a year ago after a public run on deposits sparked by news it was saddled with about $2.7 billion in bad loans.
